$sources: BSL Enforcement Order Art. 82-3: the horizontal capacity Qu of each storey at least the required capacity Qun = Ds Fes Qud
MOC Notification No. 1792 of 1980: Art. 2 (Qud with C0 = 1.0), Art. 3-4 (Ds of steel and RC structures by the member ranks FA-FD and βu), Art. 5 (Fes = Fs Fe of Rs and Re), the member rank limits
BSL Enforcement Order Art. 82-6: the primary design's limits Rs >= 0.6, Re <= 0.15
AIJ / BSL commentary: the mean shear strength of RC members (Arakawa's mean form) and the flexural strengths of the member rank calculation
source: BSL Enforcement Order Art. 82-3 and MOC Notification 1792

sources.capacityDrift: The law asks Qu at the mechanism (the collapse mechanism of an incremental analysis); SAEngine reads it at a storey drift of 1/100 or the largest shear before (SAEngine practice, as the brief of the track: raise or lower it under Code Values)
sources.ds: MOC Notification 1792 Art. 3 (steel: the columns' and beams' rank FA-FD with the braces' share βu: 0.25-0.50) and Art. 4 (RC: the frames' rank FA-FD with the walls' share βu: 0.30-0.55), the bands βu <= 0.3, <= 0.7, above; one rank for the frames and the walls or braces (the worse of the two in the law: SAEngine takes the frames' worst member rank)
sources.systems: SAEngine practice: βu of each system (frames 0, frames with walls or braces 0.5, wall structures 1.0, braced frames 0.8); the law takes βu from the horizontal capacity the walls or braces carry: enter it under Code Values
sources.defaultRank: SAEngine practice: rank FD (the largest Ds) where the design run gives no member ranks
sources.shapeFactors: MOC Notification 1792 Art. 5: Fs = 1.0 (Rs >= 0.6), 2.0 - Rs/0.6 (Rs < 0.6); Fe = 1.0 (Re <= 0.15), linear to 1.5 at Re = 0.45, 1.5 beyond; BSL EO Art. 82-6: Rs >= 0.6, Re <= 0.15 for the buildings of route 2
sources.memberRanks: MOC Notification 1792 Art. 4 (RC columns: h0/D at least 2.5 / 2.0, σ0/Fc at most 0.35 / 0.45 / 0.55, pt at most 0.8 / 1.0 %, τu/Fc at most 0.1 / 0.125 / 0.15 for FA / FB / FC; beams τu/Fc at most 0.15 / 0.2 for FA / FB; a member failing in shear FD) and Art. 3 (steel width-thickness ratios × √(235/F): H columns flange 9.5 / 12 / 15.5, web 43 / 45 / 48; box columns 33 / 37 / 48; pipes 50 / 70 / 100 × 235/F; H beams flange 9 / 11 / 15.5, web 60 / 65 / 71)
sources.shearStrength: The mean shear strength (Arakawa mean form of the AIJ and BSL commentary): Qsu = {0.068 pt^0.23 (Fc + 18) / (M/(Q d) + 0.12) + 0.85 √(pw σwy) + 0.1 σ0} b j, 1 <= M/(Q d) <= 3, pw <= 1.2 %; the flexural strengths Mu = 0.9 at σy d (beams), 0.8 at σy D + 0.5 N D (1 - N/(b D Fc)) (columns), σy = 1.1 F (the bars' strength in the ultimate calculation of MLIT Notification 2464)
